description: Shared contract between the request-intelligence agent, the catalog/verification/optimizer service and the frontend. Full field semantics: docs/procurement-engine.md. A complete real response: examples/response-60k-setup.json.

createPlan.sideEffects: None. Prepares a plan only; never creates, authorizes or captures a PayPal payment.

ProcurementRequest.rawQuery: string, optional — the user's original words, for traceability
ProcurementRequest.budgetINR: number, required, > 0, at most 2 decimals — maximum total basket cost incl. shipping
ProcurementRequest.requiredCategories: array, required, non-empty — [{ category: string, quantity: integer 1..100 }], no duplicate categories
ProcurementRequest.hardConstraints: object, optional — { <category in requiredCategories>: { <supported constraint key>: value } }. Unsupported keys are rejected (400). See GET /api/procurement/contract
ProcurementRequest.weights: object, optional — { quality, reliability, delivery }, each 0..1, must sum to 1 (±0.001). Not normalized. If omitted, defaults 0.45/0.35/0.20 are used and a warning is returned

example.rawQuery: I need a complete setup for coding and gaming under ₹60,000. I already own a laptop. I need a 144 Hz monitor, keyboard, mouse and headphones. Prioritize value for money, reliability and delivery within a week.

ProcurementPlan.planId: string — deterministic hash of the validated request + catalog version
ProcurementPlan.strategies: object keyed by StrategyKey — only strategies with a distinct feasible basket appear; empty object when INFEASIBLE
ProcurementPlan.omittedStrategies: [{ strategyKey, reason }] — strategies left out because they would duplicate another plan or none exists
ProcurementPlan.infeasibility: null | { reasons[], cheapestPossibleTotalINR, cheapestByCategoryINR, categoryDiagnostics[], suggestions[] }
ProcurementPlan.rejectedProducts: [{ productId, name, category, unitPriceINR, rejectedReason, rejectionType, failedChecks[], unknownChecks[], dataOrigin }]

Strategy.objectiveSummary: string — what the strategy actually optimizes
Strategy.paypalSettlementUSD: null — set only by the PayPal/FX flow; the optimizer never estimates it
Strategy.verificationLevel: EvidenceStatus — weakest evidence status among the items
Strategy.constraintSummary: { budgetCheck, categoryCoverageCheck, mandatorySpecCheck, deliveryCheck, stockCheck, priceDataCheck } each PASSED | FAILED
Strategy.tradeOff: ALTERNATIVE only — { categoriesChanged[], costDifferenceINR, compositeScoreDifference, summary }
Strategy.items: Item[] — one per product line; a category may have several lines (mixed SKUs)

Item.name: string
Item.shippingINR: number — charged once per line, not per unit
Item.scores: { quality: number|null, reliability: number|null, delivery, composite }
Item.verification: { status: EvidenceStatus, dataOrigin, sourceLookup, checksPassed: string[], warnings: string[], sourceUrl: string|null, lastCheckedISO: string|null }

changesFromOriginalDraft: verification.status 'VERIFIED' is now reserved for fresh, source-backed data; demo items are 'UNVERIFIED_DEMO_DATA'. Frontend must not show a verified badge for other statuses.
BEST_VALUE objectiveSummary no longer claims to maximize quality-to-price ratio; price is a budget limit and tie-breaker unless the team agrees to add a value weight.

Added fields (additive, nothing renamed): requestId, rawQuery, catalog, scoring, search, omittedStrategies, infeasibility, subtotalINR, shippingTotalINR, scoreBreakdown, verificationLevel, constraintSummary.stockCheck, constraintSummary.priceDataCheck, tradeOff, item.brand/deliveryDays/warrantyMonths/scores, rejectedProducts[].rejectionType/failedChecks/unknownChecks/dataOrigin.
